title: Capacity of participants and consortium as a whole
content:
# B.3.2 Capacity of participants and consortium as a whole

## One consortium built as the genome-to-space chain

The topic asks for one observation chain, from molecules to satellites, not a set of parallel tools. The consortium is assembled as that chain. Twelve partners, P01 to P12, cover the six objectives and the seven work packages. Each observation layer carries one lead, and each demonstration realm carries one lead. Every partner's participation is an operator assumption, so the coverage below is design intent rather than confirmed membership.

## Disciplinary and inter-disciplinary coverage

The consortium spans twelve disciplines, joined along the integration chain.

| Partner | Discipline | Contribution to the action |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | plant physiology and stress metabolomics | in-situ physiological and metabolomic measurement; statistical design and leakage-safe validation |
| P02 | geoinformatics and remote sensing | sensor harmonisation from field spectroscopy through aerial survey to satellite earth observation |
| P03 | agronomy | the multi-season field archive and the terrestrial case along the agricultural pressure gradient |
| P04 | software engineering | reproducible pipelines, provenance and the decision-support surface |
| P05 | farm-management information systems | the route carrying biodiversity indicators into farm-management tools |
| P06 | horticultural research | transfer of the measurement protocols to a second production context and country |
| P07 | freshwater ecology | the freshwater case and the floodplain and riparian ecotone observations |
| P08 | marine and coastal science | the marine case and the marine occurrence and reporting records |
| P09 | biodiversity genomics | the genomic, transcriptomic and environmental DNA layer and the omics metadata standard |
| P10 | biodiversity data infrastructure | the crosswalks, the metadata profile and the open-science-cloud link |
| P11 | socio-ecological systems | pressure analysis, socio-economic drivers and policy-reporting needs |
| P12 | earth observation analytics and AI | European-scale habitat mapping and biodiversity trend prediction |

The inter-disciplinary join is the project's method, not a by-product. Omics (P01, P09), in-situ ecology (P03, P07, P08), remote sensing (P02, P12), data infrastructure (P10, P04) and socio-ecological analysis (P11) meet on one metadata standard and one pressure gradient.

## Social sciences and humanities, open science and gender

P11 carries the social-science capability. It analyses the socio-economic drivers behind each case and translates reporting obligations into data needs. This answers the scope requirement to take socio-economic pressures into account.

Open science rests on P10 and P04. P10 holds FAIR metadata practice and the integration of services into the European open science cloud. P04 holds the provenance tracking that makes the pipelines reproducible. The compliance profile requires FAIR data and links to the open science cloud and the common data spaces, and these two partners carry that duty.

The compliance profile requires a gender equality plan and an ethics review. No partner records dedicated expertise in the gender dimension of research content. This is a gap, flagged rather than concealed: the gender-of-R&I expertise must be added, through a partner or an advisory role, before submission.

## Access to critical infrastructure

Each activity rests on infrastructure a partner already operates, so the project reworks existing capacity rather than building it.
- Field and laboratory: P03's multi-season field-experiment archive and precision-agriculture instrumentation; P01's metabolomics platform; P09's sequencing, bioinformatics and reference libraries.
- Observation: P02's hyperspectral imaging, field spectroscopy and uncrewed aerial survey; P12's scalable cloud processing for European-scale earth observation.
- Data facilities: P10's national species-occurrence data facility, which publishes to a global biodiversity data facility; P08's route to a global marine biodiversity data facility.
- Uptake: P05's multi-country user network of agricultural holdings.

The project also reaches external infrastructure through named interfaces. P10 holds cooperation with the in-situ data collection frameworks the topic names, and the open-science-cloud and common-data-space link. P02 and P12 hold coordination with the space-agency earth observation programme the topic names. Access to all of this is assumed, because no partner's participation is confirmed.

## How the partners complement one another

Three chains make the consortium one system.

Genome to space. P09 contributes the genomic and transcriptomic record and P01 the metabolomic record. These join the in-situ plots of P03, P07 and P08, the aerial and satellite layer of P02, and the European-scale maps of P12, through the metadata standard P10 and P09 define.

Catchment to coast. The three realms sit on one agricultural pressure gradient. P03 runs farmland and grassland, P07 the freshwater ecotones receiving the runoff, and P08 the coastal waters downstream. A harmonisation decision taken in farmland is tested again in each realm.

Pressure to sector. P11 analyses the pressures and the reporting needs. P10 and P04 turn the outputs into a decision surface. P05 carries the indicators into farm-management tools, and P08 and P07 carry the marine and freshwater indicators to the competent authorities.

## Valid role and resources for each participant

Each partner holds one management role, and the twelve roles do not overlap. P01 coordinates. P02 is scientific and technical coordinator. P10 leads data management and interoperability, P09 the omics integration, P12 the analytics and prediction, and P04 the software and reproducibility. P03, P07 and P08 lead the terrestrial, freshwater and marine cases. P05 leads exploitation and uptake, P11 policy and stakeholder work, and P06 the protocol transfer.

Resources follow the role. Until the consortium agrees the effort split, each role is justified by the declared capability that carries it. Person-months and the detailed budget are set with the validated lump-sum budget, which an external planner computes, so no effort or cost figure is fixed here. Detailed intellectual-property access rights belong in the consortium agreement, which is not yet drafted; the grant-default allocation applies until then.

## Industrial and commercial involvement

Three partners are SMEs, and they own the project's routes to use. P04 engineers the reproducible processing and the decision-support surface. P05 carries biodiversity indicators into farm-management tools through its multi-country user network. P12 holds the European-scale habitat mapping and trend-prediction product.

This involvement matches the exploitation measures in section 2.2. The scope names agriculture as a sector that biodiversity data must reach, and P05's existing network is the channel that reaches it. P12 and P04 own the analytical and software products the exploitation plan carries forward.

## Other countries and international organisations

Every partner is a beneficiary and an independent legal entity, placed in a Member State or an Associated Country slot. Four slots are Member State and two are Associated Country, P08 and P11. Member States and Associated Countries are both funding limbs under the General Annexes, so both Associated-Country partners are eligible for funding without a separate case. The essentiality clause applies only to an entity outside those limbs, and no participant sits outside them, so it is not triggered here.

No participation restriction binds the consortium. The destination, Biodiversity and ecosystem services, is on the list that exempts a Research and Innovation Action from the restriction on entities established in China, and no partner sits in a restricted country. The consortium holds no affiliated entities, so none is counted towards the composition minimum.

## What is assumed, and what it costs

The composition condition is met only under assumption. The six derived partners, P01 to P06, span two Member State slots, one short of the Tier 1 minimum. Every partner that adds a third country, P07 to P12, is a fictional gap partner carried as an operator declaration. The condition therefore holds on the strength of those declarations, not on confirmed membership.

Two consequences follow for implementation. The freshwater realm rests on P07 alone and the marine realm on P08 alone, so losing either withdraws a realm rather than delaying it. The geography is thin: ten of the twelve partners sit in three country slots. Both are carried as risks in section 3.1 and must be resolved before the grant agreement.
